framework.name: CyberFundamentals Framework (CCN-CERT)
framework.description: The Belgian CyberFundamentals Framework 2025 — mandatory cybersecurity baseline for operators of essential services (OES) under the NIS2 transposition (Loi 2024). Based on NIST CSF 2.0 structure. Four assurance levels: Small, Basic, Important, Essential. Covers 6 functions: Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover.

objects.title: Organisational mission and cybersecurity risk management
objects.description: The organisational mission is understood and informs cybersecurity risk management.

objects.title: Stakeholder needs and expectations for cybersecurity risk management
objects.description: Internal and external stakeholders are understood, and their needs and expectations regarding cybersecurity risk management are understood and considered.

objects.title: Legal, regulatory, and contractual cybersecurity requirements
objects.description: Legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements regarding cybersecurity are understood and managed.

objects.title: Dependencies on external capabilities and services
objects.description: Outcomes, capabilities, and services that the organisation depends on are understood and communicated.

objects.title: Risk management objectives
objects.description: Risk management objectives are established and agreed to by organisational stakeholders.

objects.title: Risk appetite and risk tolerance
objects.description: Risk appetite and risk tolerance statements are established, communicated, and maintained.

objects.title: Cybersecurity in enterprise risk management
objects.description: Cybersecurity risk management activities and outcomes are included in enterprise risk management processes.

objects.title: Leadership accountability for cybersecurity risk
objects.description: Organisational leadership is responsible and accountable for cybersecurity risk and fosters a culture that is risk-aware, ethical, and continually improving.

objects.title: Cybersecurity roles, responsibilities, and authorities
objects.description: Roles, responsibilities, and authorities related to cybersecurity risk management are established, communicated, understood, and enforced.

objects.title: Cybersecurity risk management policy
objects.description: Policy for managing cybersecurity risks is established based on organisational context, cybersecurity strategy, and priorities and is communicated and enforced.

objects.title: Supply chain risk management programme
objects.description: A cybersecurity supply chain risk management program, strategy, objectives, policies, and processes are established and agreed to by organisational stakeholders.

objects.title: Supplier risk monitoring
objects.description: The risks posed by a supplier, their products and services, and other third parties are understood, recorded, prioritised, assessed, responded to, and monitored over the course of the relationship.

objects.title: Hardware asset inventory
objects.description: Inventories of hardware managed by the organisation are maintained.

objects.title: Software, services, and systems inventory
objects.description: Inventories of software, services, and systems managed by the organisation are maintained.

objects.title: Asset prioritisation
objects.description: Assets are prioritised based on classification, criticality, resources, and impact on the mission.

objects.title: Data inventory and metadata
objects.description: Inventories of data and corresponding metadata for designated data types are maintained.

objects.title: Vulnerability identification and recording
objects.description: Vulnerabilities in assets are identified, validated, and recorded.

objects.title: Threat identification
objects.description: Internal and external threats to the organisation are identified and recorded.

objects.title: Risk understanding and prioritisation
objects.description: Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods, and impacts are used to understand inherent risk and inform risk response prioritisation.

objects.title: Improvements from security tests and exercises
objects.description: Improvements are identified from security tests and exercises, including those done in coordination with suppliers and relevant third parties.

objects.title: Identity and credential management
objects.description: Identities and credentials for authorised users, services, and hardware are managed by the organisation.

objects.title: Authentication of users, services, and hardware
objects.description: Users, services, and hardware are authenticated.

objects.title: Access permissions and least privilege
objects.description: Access permissions, entitlements, and authorisations are defined in a policy, managed, enforced, and reviewed, and incorporate the principles of least privilege and separation of duties.

objects.title: Data-at-rest protection
objects.description: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-at-rest are protected.

objects.title: Data-in-transit protection
objects.description: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-in-transit are protected.

objects.title: Data backup
objects.description: Backups of data are created, protected, maintained, and tested.

objects.title: Configuration management
objects.description: Configuration management practices are established and applied.

objects.title: Network and environment access control
objects.description: Networks and environments are protected from unauthorised logical access and usage.

objects.title: Network monitoring
objects.description: Networks and network services are monitored to find potentially adverse events.

objects.title: Hardware and software monitoring
objects.description: Computing hardware and software, runtime environments, and their data are monitored to find potentially adverse events.

objects.title: Adverse event analysis
objects.description: Potentially adverse events are analysed to better understand associated activities.

objects.title: Incident declaration
objects.description: Incidents are declared when adverse events meet the defined incident criteria.

objects.title: Incident response plan execution
objects.description: The incident response plan is executed in coordination with relevant third parties once an incident is declared.

objects.title: Incident categorisation and prioritisation
objects.description: Incidents are categorised and prioritised.

objects.title: Incident analysis and root cause
objects.description: Analysis is performed to establish what has taken place during an incident and the root cause of the incident.

objects.title: Incident stakeholder notification
objects.description: Internal and external stakeholders are notified of incidents.

objects.title: Incident containment
objects.description: Incidents are contained.

objects.title: Recovery plan execution
objects.description: The recovery portion of the incident response plan is executed once initiated from the incident response process.

objects.title: Recovery action selection and execution
objects.description: Recovery actions are selected, scoped, prioritised, and performed.

objects.title: Integrity verification and service restoration
objects.description: The integrity of restored assets is verified, systems and services are restored, and normal operating status is confirmed.

objects.title: Recovery progress communication
objects.description: Recovery activities and progress in restoring operational capabilities are communicated to designated internal and external stakeholders.
